subject: Embed migration rollout — tasks, index backfill schedule, and rerank eval criteria
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference>
To: Emma Jordan <emma.jordan@searchly.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Embed migration rollout — tasks, index backfill schedule, and rerank eval criteria

Hi Emma,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our call, attached is the initial migration playbook and a seed index CSV that maps your current collection IDs -> candidate chunks for re-ingestion. We put together an implementation-first plan so your engineering team can run the backfill with minimal downtime and the CS/PLG teams can validate quality.

High-level ask: please confirm which vector DB you want to use for production (you mentioned either VectorCorp-hosted or an in-house Milvus cluster). The migration plan assumes VectorCorp will accept streaming bulk loads and that we can do a short canary subset before a full backfill. If you prefer in-house, we'll provide the same connectors but the backfill window and throughput targets will change.

Proposed timeline (please confirm availability):
1) Week of Jun 22 — Canaries: 5% of the corpus (seed list attached) + rerank eval on holdout queries.
2) Week of Jun 29 — Full backfill in 48–72 hour window (rolling batches, low-traffic window).
3) Jul 6 — Cutover and two-week monitoring (latency/cost/quality dashboards).

Implementation tasks (owners in parens):
- Finalize vector DB and configuration (index type, dimension, compression) (Searchly + VectorCorp ops)
- Freeze embeddings model version (if changed, re-embed and re-hash id mapping) (Searchly eng)
- Prepare backfill export (chunk size, TTL, metadata) (Searchly eng / Redwood connectors)
- Run canary backfill + smoke tests (Redwood + VectorCorp)
- Rerank evaluation: generate holdout queries, annotation plan, run baseline (BM25) vs embeddings+reranker (Redwood research + Searchly PM)
- Rollout: canary -> staged -> full with rollback threshold defined by NDCG/MRR deltas

Rerank eval details we need your input on:
- Holdout set size: 300–500 queries (would like to use existing Searchly usage logs to sample)
- Relevance labels: binary vs graded (we recommend 3-level graded relevance for better signal)
- Primary metrics: NDCG@10, MRR, and recall@100. Define minimum acceptable delta vs baseline for go/no-go.

Attachments: redwood_embed_migration_playbook_v1.pdf (playbook with task checklist), index_seed_list_searchly.csv (5% seed set for canary).

Can you confirm: 1) Vector DB choice, 2) preferred canary week (Jun 22 or Jun 29), 3) whether Searchly will provide an anonymized query log extract for sampling?

If that works, I will schedule a 30-minute technical sync next week (Marissa and Karthik to lead on the connector/backfill details).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this into your staging environment.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi Lauren — thanks for the clear plan and the docs.

Short answers:
- We prefer VectorCorp-hosted for production due to existing enterprise support, but we need SLA details around write/ingest throughput and read tail-latency (p95/p99).
- Canary week: Jun 22 works for us if VectorCorp can do the 5% ingest in that slot.
- We can provide anonymized query logs (search logs from last 90 days) — I will ask our infra to produce a sanitized extract by Friday.

A few questions for your team and VectorCorp ops (cc'd):
- How do you handle idempotency for backfills if a chunk is re-sent? Any dedup logic?
- Will we be able to run side-by-side queries (current production index vs candidate index) for the rerank eval without traffic cutover? We would like to run parallel experiments.

VectorCorp ops — can you confirm write SLA and whether you support a streaming bulk ingest API + idempotent upserts?

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Embed migration rollout — tasks, index backfill schedule, and rerank eval criteria

On Thu, Jun 18, 2026 at 09:08 AM Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.inference> wrote:
> Hi Emma,
> 
> Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our call, attached is the initial migration playbook...

Emma — quick technical notes / proposals from Redwood infra side to unblock the canary and evaluation:

1) Vector DB considerations (short):
- Index type: IVF-PQ or HNSW are both viable; HNSW gives faster recall at the cost of bigger memory. If VectorCorp offers GPU-backed FAISS we should use IVF-PQ with OPQ for cost savings.
- Dimension & compression: Keep your current embedding dim (1536) in the canary. We can test 8-bit quantized vectors during canary to measure latency/cost tradeoffs but keep a full-precision copy for the reranker evaluation to avoid confounding quality results.
- Idempotency: our connector supports a per-chunk checksum + upsert id. If the backend supports upsert semantics we'll send chunk_id + checksum, otherwise we'll manage dedupe client-side and mark processed offsets in a checkpoint table.

2) Backfill execution plan (canary -> full):
- Export: create NDJSON export with chunk_id, text, metadata, embedding_version. Use the attached seed CSV for canary.
- Canary: push 5% in parallel streams (4 workers x 8 threads), validate counts, run smoke queries. Expected ingest time: ~3–6 hours for 5% on VectorCorp infra (subject to their write SLA).
- Full: backfill in 24–72 hours depending on chosen parallelism and write throughput; we'll provide a progress dashboard.

3) Rerank evaluation (detailed):
- Holdout queries: 400 queries sampled from search logs (stratified by query length and frequency).
- Labeling: crowdsource a 3-level relevance (2 = highly relevant, 1 = somewhat, 0 = not). We recommend 3 labels per query-doc pair, majority vote aggregation.
- Baselines: BM25 (current prod), embeddings kNN (candidate), and embeddings + cross-encoder reranker (candidate).
- Metrics & thresholds: NDCG@10 and MRR are primary. Minimum acceptable improvement: NDCG@10 >= +0.06 over BM25 or MRR >= +0.05 depending on search intent segment. If thresholds aren't met we recommend tuning the reranker or reverting to embeddings-only.
- Statistical testing: paired bootstrap for confidence intervals; require p<0.05 for promotion.

4) Parallel eval strategy: we can run side-by-side (non-traffic) evaluation by duplicating the query stream against the candidate index and capturing logs, or run a small percentage of live traffic (1–2%) with A/B measurement. Side-by-side offline first, then 1% live A/B for sanity check.

Action items I will take this week:
- Prepare an evaluation harness (scripts and sample annotations) and share a short runbook.
- Add instrumentation to the playbook for perf/cost dashboards and rollback triggers.
- Coordinate with VectorCorp for write throughput numbers; Karthik will be the internal contact for connector configuration.

Attachments referenced again: redwood_embed_migration_playbook_v1.pdf, index_seed_list_searchly.csv

Marissa Cole
Staff Engineer, Inference Integrations
